Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Burning sensation on urination (dysuria) with mild lower abdominal cramping for a few days; occasional blood in urine earlier today; urine odor described as 'weird'.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms started a few days ago; not improved.
- Associated symptoms: No fever, no back pain, no nausea/vomiting, bowel function normal.
- Urinary symptoms: Not reported as increased frequency.
- Sexual history: Sexually active with a regular partner.
- Contraception: Uses condoms.
- Pregnancy: Consideration raised; advised pregnancy test if symptoms persist or to rule out pregnancy.
- Menstrual history: Last period a couple of weeks ago (patient) vs three weeks ago (clinician) – discrepancy noted.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Medications: No regular medications; has used over-the-counter bicarbonate for pain with no relief.
- Allergies: Clindamycin — causes swelling (documented severe allergy).
- Social history: Student; lives with friends near college; non-smoker; drinks alcohol on weekends.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical examination: Not documented (examination planned but not reported).
- Investigations: Not performed at this visit (no results reported).

Assessment & Plan:
1. Issue: Urinary tract infection (simple UTI)
   - Assessment: Simple UTI (bladder infection) suspected based on dysuria with mild suprapubic pain and hematuria/non-severe symptoms; no fever or flank pain reported.
   - Differential diagnoses: Urethritis; vaginitis; sexually transmitted infection; pyelonephritis (if symptoms progress or fever/back pain develop).
   - Investigations planned: Consider pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy if concern persists; follow-up if symptoms do not improve by end of week.
   - Treatment planned: Antibiotic therapy
     - Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim; three-day course; 1 tablet twice daily (route not explicitly documented for chosen drug).
     - Additional home care: Increase fluids; cranberry juice can be considered.
     - Sexual activity: Advise avoiding sex while symptoms persist; continue barrier contraception.
     - Follow-up: If not improved by end of the week, contact/return for re-evaluation; monitor for fever, back pain, or worsening illness (signals for possible ascending infection).
   - Referrals: None.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs; physical exam findings; urinalysis results; urine culture results; explicit medication choice (Drug name if nitrofurantoin vs trimethoprim), and exact route documented; pregnancy test result if performed.
- Internal conflicts: Patient-reported last menstrual period (couple of weeks ago) conflicts with clinician’s note of three weeks ago.
- Transcript quality: Generally coherent; no major inaudible segments noted.
